Standards Codification (ASC) Topic&#160;842, &#8220;Leases,&#8221; (Topic&#160;842) on January&#160;1, 2019, as described below in &#8220;Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January&#160;1, 2019.&#8221; Accordingly, our lease accounting policy has been revised to reflect the adoption of this standard.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">6</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;" href="#sD7A668EF921D5B8880C41A37391EB323"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;">Table of Contents</span></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">VALERO ENERGY CORPORATION</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">CONDENSED NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</span></div></div><div><br/></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-61A60E9DA77D5C8187711877AB58172F-3" continuedAt="TextSelection-61A60E9DA77D5C8187711877AB58172F-4"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-66B9384AA9502EAB7A83DEBB575D5F06-2" continuedAt="TextSelection-66B9384AA9502EAB7A83DEBB575D5F06-3"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:22px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Revised Policy</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We evaluate if a contract is or contains a lease at inception of the contract. If we determine that a contract is or contains a lease, we recognize a right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability at the commencement date of the lease based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term. The present value of the lease payments is determined by using the implicit rate when readily determinable, or if not, our incremental borrowing rate for a term similar to the duration of the lease based on information available at the commencement date. Lease terms include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that we will exercise those options.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities for leasing arrangements with terms greater than one&#160;year. Except for the marine transportation asset class, we account for lease and non-lease components in a contract as a single lease component for all classes of underlying assets. Our marine transportation contracts include non-lease components such as maintenance and crew costs. We allocate the consideration in these contracts based on pricing information provided by the third-party broker.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></ix:continuation><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-66B9384AA9502EAB7A83DEBB575D5F06-3">Expense for an operating lease is recognized as a single lease cost on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in the appropriate income statement line item based on the leased asset&#8217;s function. Amortization expense of a finance lease ROU asset is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in &#8220;depreciation and amortization expense,&#8221; and interest expense is incurred based on the carrying value of the lease liability and reflected in &#8220;interest and debt expense, net of capitalized interest.&#8221;</ix:continuation></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-0-wk-Fact-E2FAD15579BD5943B5FF585BD2ADCA71" continuedAt="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-1" escape="true">Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January</ix:nonNumeric></span><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-1" continuedAt="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-2"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">1, 2019</span></ix:continuation></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-2" continuedAt="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-3"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Topic&#160;842 </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">As previously noted, we adopted the provisions of Topic&#160;842 on January&#160;1, 2019. Topic&#160;842 increases the transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. Topic&#160;842 supersedes previous lease accounting requirements under FASB ASC Topic&#160;840, &#8220;Leases,&#8221; (Topic&#160;840). We adopted Topic&#160;842 using the optional transition method that permits us to apply the new disclosure requirements beginning in 2019 and continue to present comparative period information as required under Topic&#160;840; however, we did not have a cumulative-effect adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings at the date of adoption.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">In addition, we elected the transition practical expedient package that permits us to not reassess our prior conclusions about lease identification, lease classification, and initial direct costs under the new standard, as well as the practical expedient that permits us to not assess existing land easements under the new standard. See &#8220;Leases&#8221; above for a discussion of our accounting policy affected by our adoption of Topic&#160;842. Also see </span><span style="font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;4</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for information on our leases.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">In preparation for the adoption of Topic&#160;842, we enhanced our contracting and lease evaluation systems and related processes, and we developed a new lease accounting system to capture our leases and support the required disclosures. We integrated our lease accounting system with our general ledger and modified our related procurement and payment processes.</span></div><div The transaction price for our remaining term contracts includes a fixed component and variable consideration (i.e., a commodity price), both of which are allocated entirely to a wholly unsatisfied promise to transfer a distinct good that forms part of a single performance obligation. Accordingly, we created a new reportable segment &#8212; renewable diesel &#8212; because of the growing importance of renewable fuels in the market and the growth of our investments in renewable fuels production. The renewable diesel segment includes the operations of DGD, which were transferred from the refining segment on January&#160;1, 2019. Also effective January&#160;1, 2019, we no longer have a VLP segment, and we include the operations of VLP in our refining segment. This change was made because of the Merger Transaction with VLP, as described in </span><span style="font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;2</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, and the resulting change in how we manage VLP&#8217;s operations. Our prior period segment information has been retrospectively adjusted to reflect our current segment presentation.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We have </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span><ix:nonFraction id="d2933580e704-wk-Fact-0A0FD9BACB1F5A379A85F446AB46AA99" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" unitRef="segment" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;reportable segments &#8211; refining, ethanol, and renewable diesel. Each segment is a strategic business unit that offers different products and services by employing unique technologies and marketing strategies and whose operations and operating performance are managed and evaluated separately. The majority of these commitments matured on or before </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">April&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Environmental Compliance Program Price Risk</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are exposed to market risk related to the volatility in the price of credits needed to comply with various governmental and regulatory environmental compliance programs. To manage this risk, we enter into contracts to purchase these credits when prices are deemed favorable. Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These countries set annual quotas for the percentage of biofuels that must be blended into the motor fuels consumed in these countries. As a producer of motor fuels from petroleum, we are obligated to blend biofuels into the products we produce at a rate that is at least equal to the applicable quota. To the degree we are unable to blend at the applicable rate, we must purchase biofuel credits (primarily RINs in the U.S.). We are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits, and we manage that risk by purchasing biofuel credits when prices are deemed favorable. The cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d2935693e1228-wk-Fact-2E7850070C46590F80B43F087BD07C16" name="us-gaap:CostDirectMaterial" contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD_srt_ProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaap_OilAndGasRefiningAndMarketingMember" unitRef="usd" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">91</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d2935693e1232-wk-Fact-D0C728BCD5625E5A8B72B9A069739008" name="us-gaap:CostDirectMaterial" contextRef="FD2018Q1YTD_srt_ProductOrServiceAxis_us-gaap_OilAndGasRefiningAndMarketingMember" unitRef="usd" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">206</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, respectively. In addition, any major upgrades in any of our operating facilities could require material additional expenditures to comply with environmental laws and regulations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Tax Matters</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The IRS has ongoing audits related to our U.S. federal income tax returns from 2012 through 2015. We did not have a significant change to our uncertain tax positions upon the settlement of the 2010 and 2011 combined audit. The remaining cash held by that subsidiary, as well as our other international subsidiaries, will be permanently reinvested in our operations in those countries.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Concentration of Customers</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Our operations have a concentration of customers in the refining industry and customers who are refined petroleum product wholesalers and retailers. Accordingly, they do not include all of the information and notes required by U.S.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments considered necessary for a fair presentation have been included. All such adjustments are of a normal recurring nature unless disclosed otherwise. Operating results for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the year ending &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The balance sheet as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; has been derived from our audited financial statements as of that date. For further information, refer to our financial statements and notes thereto included in our annual report on Form&#160;10-K for the year ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Reclassifications&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Effective January&#160;1, 2019, we revised our reportable segments to reflect a new reportable segment &#x2014; renewable diesel. The renewable diesel segment includes the operations of Diamond Green Diesel Holdings LLC (DGD), our consolidated joint venture as discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, which were transferred from the refining segment. Also effective January&#160;1, 2019, we no longer have a VLP segment, and we now include the operations of Valero Energy Partners LP and its consolidated subsidiaries (VLP) in our refining segment. Our prior period segment information has been retrospectively adjusted to reflect our current segment presentation. See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; regarding our merger with VLP, which occurred on January&#160;10, 2019, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;11&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for segment information.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Significant Accounting Policies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Use of Estimates&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ from those estimates. On an ongoing basis, we review our estimates based on currently available information. Changes in facts and circumstances may result in revised estimates.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Background&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We adopted the provisions of Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) Topic&#160;842, &#x201c;Leases,&#x201d; (Topic&#160;842) on January&#160;1, 2019, as described below in &#x201c;Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January&#160;1, 2019.&#x201d; Accordingly, our lease accounting policy has been revised to reflect the adoption of this standard.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:22px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Revised Policy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We evaluate if a contract is or contains a lease at inception of the contract. If we determine that a contract is or contains a lease, we recognize a right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability at the commencement date of the lease based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term. The present value of the lease payments is determined by using the implicit rate when readily determinable, or if not, our incremental borrowing rate for a term similar to the duration of the lease based on information available at the commencement date. Lease terms include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that we will exercise those options.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities for leasing arrangements with terms greater than one&#160;year. Except for the marine transportation asset class, we account for lease and non-lease components in a contract as a single lease component for all classes of underlying assets. Our marine transportation contracts include non-lease components such as maintenance and crew costs. We allocate the consideration in these contracts based on pricing information provided by the third-party broker.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Expense for an operating lease is recognized as a single lease cost on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in the appropriate income statement line item based on the leased asset&#x2019;s function. Amortization expense of a finance lease ROU asset is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in &#x201c;depreciation and amortization expense,&#x201d; and interest expense is incurred based on the carrying value of the lease liability and reflected in &#x201c;interest and debt expense, net of capitalized interest.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;1, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Topic&#160;842 &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As previously noted, we adopted the provisions of Topic&#160;842 on January&#160;1, 2019. Topic&#160;842 increases the transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. Topic&#160;842 supersedes previous lease accounting requirements under FASB ASC Topic&#160;840, &#x201c;Leases,&#x201d; (Topic&#160;840). We adopted Topic&#160;842 using the optional transition method that permits us to apply the new disclosure requirements beginning in 2019 and continue to present comparative period information as required under Topic&#160;840; however, we did not have a cumulative-effect adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings at the date of adoption.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In addition, we elected the transition practical expedient package that permits us to not reassess our prior conclusions about lease identification, lease classification, and initial direct costs under the new standard, as well as the practical expedient that permits us to not assess existing land easements under the new standard. See &#x201c;Leases&#x201d; above for a discussion of our accounting policy affected by our adoption of Topic&#160;842. Also see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for information on our leases.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In preparation for the adoption of Topic&#160;842, we enhanced our contracting and lease evaluation systems and related processes, and we developed a new lease accounting system to capture our leases and support the required disclosures. We integrated our lease accounting system with our general ledger and modified our related procurement and payment processes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Adoption of this standard resulted in (i)&#160;the recognition of ROU assets and lease liabilities for our operating leases of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.3&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, (ii)&#160;the derecognition of existing assets under construction of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$539&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; related to a build-to-suit lease arrangement with respect to the MVP Terminal (see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; under &#x201c;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Commitments&#x2014;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;MVP &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Terminal&#x201d;), and (iii)&#160;the presentation of new disclosures about our leasing activities beginning in the first quarter of 2019. Adoption of this standard did not impact our results of operations or liquidity, and our accounting for finance leases is substantially unchanged.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Other&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In addition to the adoption of Topic&#160;842 discussed above, we adopted the following Accounting Standards Update (ASU) during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. Our adoption of this ASU did not affect our financial statements or related disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;div     <us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD"
      id="TextSelection-66B9384AA9502EAB7A83DEBB575D5F06-0-wk-Fact-05D1F738F1CC5AD56BB7DEBE2AFC9CE4">Leases&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Background&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We adopted the provisions of Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) Topic&#160;842, &#x201c;Leases,&#x201d; (Topic&#160;842) on January&#160;1, 2019, as described below in &#x201c;Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January&#160;1, 2019.&#x201d; Accordingly, our lease accounting policy has been revised to reflect the adoption of this standard.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:22px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Revised Policy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We evaluate if a contract is or contains a lease at inception of the contract. If we determine that a contract is or contains a lease, we recognize a right-of-use (ROU) asset and lease liability at the commencement date of the lease based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term. The present value of the lease payments is determined by using the implicit rate when readily determinable, or if not, our incremental borrowing rate for a term similar to the duration of the lease based on information available at the commencement date. Lease terms include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that we will exercise those options.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities for leasing arrangements with terms greater than one&#160;year. Except for the marine transportation asset class, we account for lease and non-lease components in a contract as a single lease component for all classes of underlying assets. Our marine transportation contracts include non-lease components such as maintenance and crew costs. We allocate the consideration in these contracts based on pricing information provided by the third-party broker.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;Expense for an operating lease is recognized as a single lease cost on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in the appropriate income statement line item based on the leased asset&#x2019;s function. Amortization expense of a finance lease ROU asset is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and reflected in &#x201c;depreciation and amortization expense,&#x201d; and interest expense is incurred based on the carrying value of the lease liability and reflected in &#x201c;interest and debt expense, net of capitalized interest.&#x201d;</us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock>
    <us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD"
      id="TextSelection-C00DF28E660D58E689F89E3BAE451A38-0-wk-Fact-E2FAD15579BD5943B5FF585BD2ADCA71">Accounting Pronouncements Adopted on January&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;1, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Topic&#160;842 &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As previously noted, we adopted the provisions of Topic&#160;842 on January&#160;1, 2019. Topic&#160;842 increases the transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing lease assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet and disclosing key information about leasing arrangements. Topic&#160;842 supersedes previous lease accounting requirements under FASB ASC Topic&#160;840, &#x201c;Leases,&#x201d; (Topic&#160;840). We adopted Topic&#160;842 using the optional transition method that permits us to apply the new disclosure requirements beginning in 2019 and continue to present comparative period information as required under Topic&#160;840; however, we did not have a cumulative-effect adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings at the date of adoption.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In addition, we elected the transition practical expedient package that permits us to not reassess our prior conclusions about lease identification, lease classification, and initial direct costs under the new standard, as well as the practical expedient that permits us to not assess existing land easements under the new standard. See &#x201c;Leases&#x201d; above for a discussion of our accounting policy affected by our adoption of Topic&#160;842. Also see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for information on our leases.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In preparation for the adoption of Topic&#160;842, we enhanced our contracting and lease evaluation systems and related processes, and we developed a new lease accounting system to capture our leases and support the required disclosures. We integrated our lease accounting system with our general ledger and modified our related procurement and payment processes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Adoption of this standard resulted in (i)&#160;the recognition of ROU assets and lease liabilities for our operating leases of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.3&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, (ii)&#160;the derecognition of existing assets under construction of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$539&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; related to a build-to-suit lease arrangement with respect to the MVP Terminal (see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; under &#x201c;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Commitments&#x2014;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;MVP &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Terminal&#x201d;), and (iii)&#160;the presentation of new disclosures about our leasing activities beginning in the first quarter of 2019. Adoption of this standard did not impact our results of operations or liquidity, and our accounting for finance leases is substantially unchanged.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Other&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;In addition to the adoption of Topic&#160;842 discussed above, we adopted the following Accounting Standards Update (ASU) during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. Our adoption of this ASU did not affect our financial statements or related disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;div     <us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD"
      id="TextSelection-762CD806A6E459B891C7739830B46F79-0-wk-Fact-4652720BBE525B6AA7253D9ECC670A0E">2.&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;MERGER WITH VLP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;On January&#160;10, 2019, we completed our acquisition of all of the outstanding publicly held common units of VLP pursuant to a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger (Merger Agreement, and together with the transactions contemplated thereby, the Merger Transaction) with VLP. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, each outstanding publicly held common unit was converted into the right to receive &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$42.25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;per common unit in cash without any interest thereon, and all such publicly traded common units were automatically canceled and ceased to exist. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, we paid aggregate merger consideration of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$950&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, which was funded with available cash on hand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Prior to the completion of the Merger Transaction, we consolidated the financial statements of VLP (see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;8&lt;/span&gt;) and reflected noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet for the portion of VLP&#x2019;s partners&#x2019; capital held by VLP&#x2019;s public common unitholders. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, VLP became our indirect wholly owned subsidiary and, as a result, we no longer reflect noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet with respect to VLP. In addition, we no longer attribute a portion of VLP&#x2019;s net income to noncontrolling interests. Because we had a controlling financial interest in VLP before the Merger Transaction and retained our controlling financial interest in VLP after the Merger Transaction, the change in our ownership interest in VLP as a result of the merger was accounted for as an equity transaction. Accordingly, we did not recognize a gain or loss on the Merger Transaction.</us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock>

Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, VLP became our indirect wholly owned subsidiary and, as a result, was no longer a VIE.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Non-Consolidated VIEs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We hold variable interests in VIEs that have not been consolidated because we are not considered the primary beneficiary. These non-consolidated VIEs are not material to our financial position or results of operations and are primarily accounted for as equity investments. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;One&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of our non-consolidated VIEs is MVP, which is described in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. disaggregated by product because this is the level of disaggregation that management has determined to be beneficial to users of our financial statements.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Receivables from Contracts with Customers&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Our receivables from contracts with customers are included in &#x201c;receivables, net&#x201d; and totaled &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$5.3&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.7&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Remaining Performance Obligations&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We have spot and term contracts with customers, the majority of which are spot contracts with no remaining performance obligations. We do not disclose remaining performance obligations for contracts that have terms of one year or less. The transaction price for our remaining term contracts includes a fixed component and variable consideration (i.e., a commodity price), both of which are allocated entirely to a wholly unsatisfied promise to transfer a distinct good that forms part of a single performance obligation. The fixed component is not material and the variable consideration is highly uncertain. Therefore, as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we have not disclosed the aggregate amount of the transaction price allocated to our remaining performance obligations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Segment Information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Effective January&#160;1, 2019, we revised our reportable segments to align with certain changes in how our chief operating decision maker manages and allocates resources to our business. Accordingly, we created a new reportable segment &#x2014; renewable diesel &#x2014; because of the growing importance of renewable fuels in the market and the growth of our investments in renewable fuels production. The renewable diesel segment includes the operations of DGD, which were transferred from the refining segment on January&#160;1, 2019. Also effective January&#160;1, 2019, we no longer have a VLP segment, and we include the operations of VLP in our refining segment. This change was made because of the Merger Transaction with VLP, as described in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, and the resulting change in how we manage VLP&#x2019;s operations. We no longer manage VLP as a business but as logistics assets that support the operations of our refining segment. Our prior period segment information has been retrospectively adjusted to reflect our current segment presentation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:30px;text-indent:-30px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We have &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;reportable segments &#x2013; refining, ethanol, and renewable diesel. Each segment is a strategic business unit that offers different products and services by employing unique technologies and marketing strategies and whose operations and operating performance are managed and evaluated separately. Operating performance is measured based on the operating income generated by the segment, which includes revenues and expenses that are directly attributable to the management of the respective segment. Intersegment sales are generally derived from transactions made at prevailing market rates. The following is a description of each segment&#x2019;s business operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;refining segment&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; includes the operations of our &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;15&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; petroleum refineries, the associated marketing activities, and logistics assets that support our refining operations. The principal products manufactured by our refineries and sold by this segment include gasolines and blendstocks, distillates, and other products.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:12px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;ethanol segment &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;includes the operations of our &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; ethanol plants, the associated marketing activities, and logistics assets that support our ethanol operations. The principal products manufactured by our ethanol plants are ethanol and distillers grains. This segment sells some ethanol to the refining segment for blending into gasoline, which is sold to that segment&#x2019;s customers as a finished gasoline product.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:12px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;renewable diesel segment&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; includes the operations of DGD, our consolidated joint venture as discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. The principal product manufactured by DGD and sold by this segment is renewable diesel. This segment sells some renewable diesel to the refining segment, which is then sold to that segment&#x2019;s customers.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:right;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;A description of our assets and liabilities recognized at fair value along with the valuation methods and inputs we used to develop their fair value measurements are as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Commodity derivative contracts consist primarily of exchange-traded futures, which are used to reduce the impact of price volatility on our results of operations and cash flows as discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. These contracts are measured at fair value using the market approach. Exchange-traded futures are valued based on quoted prices from the commodity exchange and are categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Physical purchase contracts represent the fair value of fixed-price corn purchase contracts. The fair values of these purchase contracts are measured using a market approach based on quoted prices from the commodity exchange or an independent pricing service and are categorized in Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Investments of certain benefit plans consist of investment securities held by trusts for the purpose of satisfying a portion of our obligations under certain U.S. nonqualified benefit plans. The plan assets categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy are measured at fair value using a market approach based on quoted prices from national securities exchanges. The plan assets categorized in Level&#160;3 of the fair value hierarchy represent insurance contracts, the fair value of which is provided by the insurer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Foreign currency contracts consist of foreign currency exchange and purchase contracts and foreign currency swap agreements related to our international operations to manage our exposure to exchange rate fluctuations on transactions denominated in currencies other than the local (functional) currencies of our operations. These contracts are valued based on quoted prices from the exchange and are categorized in Level&#160;1 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Environmental credit obligations represent our liability for the purchase of (i)&#160;biofuel credits (primarily Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs) in the U.S.) needed to satisfy our obligation to blend biofuels into the products we produce and (ii)&#160;emission credits under the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;California Global Warming Solutions Act&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; (the California cap-and-trade system, also known as AB&#160;32) and similar programs (collectively, the cap-and-trade systems). To the degree we are unable to blend biofuels (such as ethanol and biodiesel) at percentages required under the biofuel programs, we must purchase biofuel credits to comply with these programs. Under the cap-and-trade systems, we must purchase emission credits to comply with these systems. The liability for environmental credits is based on our deficit for such credits as of the balance sheet date, if any, after considering any credits acquired or under contract, and is equal to the product of the credits deficit and the market price of these credits as of the balance sheet date. The environmental credit obligations are categorized in Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy and are measured at fair value using the market approach based on quoted prices from an independent pricing service.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;There were no transfers into or out of Level&#160;3 for assets and liabilities held as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span We enter into derivative instruments to manage some of these risks, including derivative instruments related to the various commodities we purchase or produce, and foreign currency exchange and purchase contracts, as described below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; These derivative instruments are recorded as either assets or liabilities measured at their fair values (see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:11pt;"&gt;Note&#160;13&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;), as summarized below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Fair Values of Derivative Instruments,&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; with changes in fair value recognized currently in income. The effect of these derivative instruments on our income is summarized below under &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#x201c;Effect of Derivative Instruments on Income.&#x201d;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Commodity Price Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to market risks related to the volatility in the price of crude oil, refined petroleum products (primarily gasoline and distillate), grain (primarily corn), soybean oil, and natural gas used in our operations. To reduce the impact of price volatility on our results of operations and cash flows, we use commodity derivative instruments, such as futures and options. Our positions in commodity derivative instruments are monitored and managed on a daily basis by our risk control group to ensure compliance with our stated risk management policy that has been approved by our board of directors.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We primarily use commodity derivative instruments as economic hedges, which are not designated as hedging instruments, and we use fair value and cash flow hedges from time to time. We had no commodity derivative instruments outstanding as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, and no activity during the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; that were designated as fair value or cash flow hedges.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Our objectives for holding economic hedges are to (i)&#160;manage price volatility in certain feedstock and refined petroleum product inventories and fixed-price purchase contracts, and (ii)&#160;lock in the price of forecasted feedstock, refined petroleum product, or natural gas purchases and refined petroleum product sales at existing market prices that we deem favorable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we had the following outstanding commodity derivative instruments that were used as economic hedges, as well as commodity derivative instruments related to the physical purchase of corn at a fixed price. style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Foreign Currency Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to exchange rate fluctuations on transactions related to our international operations that are denominated in currencies other than the local (functional) currencies of our operations. To manage our exposure to these exchange rate fluctuations, we use foreign currency contracts. These contracts are not designated as hedging instruments for accounting purposes and therefore are classified as economic hedges. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we had foreign currency contracts to purchase &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$418&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollars, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.7&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollar equivalent Canadian dollars, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$300&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of U.S. dollar equivalent pounds sterling. The majority of these commitments matured on or before &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;April&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Environmental Compliance Program Price Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We are exposed to market risk related to the volatility in the price of credits needed to comply with various governmental and regulatory environmental compliance programs. To manage this risk, we enter into contracts to purchase these credits when prices are deemed favorable. Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These countries set annual quotas for the percentage of biofuels that must be blended into the motor fuels consumed in these countries. As a producer of motor fuels from petroleum, we are obligated to blend biofuels into the products we produce at a rate that is at least equal to the applicable quota. To the degree we are unable to blend at the applicable rate, we must purchase biofuel credits (primarily RINs in the U.S.). We are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits, and we manage that risk by purchasing biofuel credits when prices are deemed favorable. The cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$91&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$206&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, respectively. These amounts are reflected in cost of materials and other.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Fair Values of Derivative Instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The following tables provide information about the fair values of our derivative instruments as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; (in&#160;millions) and the line items in the balance sheets in which the fair values are reflected. See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-size:11pt;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note&#160;13&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for additional information related to the fair values of our derivative instruments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;As indicated in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-size:11pt;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note&#160;13&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, we net fair value amounts recognized for multiple similar derivative contracts executed with the same counterparty under master netting arrangements, including cash collateral assets and obligations. The following tables, however, are presented on a gross asset and gross liability basis, which results in the reflection of certain assets in liability accounts and certain liabilities in asset Risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Our price risk management activities involve the receipt or payment of fixed price commitments into the future. These transactions give rise to market risk, which is the risk that future changes in market conditions may make an instrument less valuable. We closely monitor and manage our exposure to market risk on a daily basis in accordance with policies approved by our board of directors. Market risks are monitored by our risk control group to ensure compliance with our stated risk management policy. We do not require any collateral or other security to support derivative instruments into which we enter. We also do not have any derivative instruments that require us to maintain a minimum investment-grade credit rating.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:12px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Effect of Derivative Also includes short-term, highly liquid investments that are both readily convertible to known amounts of cash and so near their maturity that they present insignificant risk of changes in value because of changes in interest rates.
